model.name: a-ladder-of-round-milliseconds
model.of: the byte at a delay-time address, and the time the copy comes back at
model.chosen_by: the range the page prints against that address

what: A ladder of round decimal milliseconds whose step changes a handful of times over the byte. Between two changes the step is constant, so the byte is walked one entry at a time and not solved.
note: Generated from the candidate this file names, and read only by src/soundings/reproduce.py. It states what the candidate predicts at every setting of the byte, so that a reading can disagree with it. Nothing here is a measurement.

how_each_range_was_arrived_at.0 - 500m: Read at all hundred and twenty-eight settings on 01 50, and at seven of them on 01 51, which agreed at every one. The step changes five times: a tenth of a millisecond to fifty, then a half, then one, then ten, then twenty.
how_each_range_was_arrived_at.0 - 100m: The first three steps are the other range's, read at bytes 1, 8, 32 and 64 on 01 40 and identical there. Where it leaves them is fixed by two further readings rather than drawn through them: byte 96 came back at forty-six milliseconds, which is the one-millisecond step still running past where the longer range leaves it, and byte 127 came back at a hundred. A single later change of step meeting both wants a step of two from byte 104, and no other round step lands on a whole setting. That is a prediction about sixty settings nothing has read, and the breakpoint is where it is falsifiable.
